memberdef.argsstring: (Section &Parent, MutableArrayRef< char > Content, orc::ExecutorAddr Address, uint64_t Alignment, uint64_t AlignmentOffset)
memberdef.name: Block

briefdescription.para: Create a defined addressable for the given content.

detaileddescription.para: The content is assumed to be writable, and the caller is responsible for ensuring that it lives for the duration of the Block's lifetime. The standard way to achieve this is to allocate it on the Graph's allocator.

briefdescription.para: Return the parent section for this block.
Returns true if this is a zero-fill block.

detaileddescription.para: If true, getSize is callable but getContent is not (the content is defined to be a sequence of zero bytes of length Size).

briefdescription.para: Returns the size of this defined addressable.
Turns this block into a zero-fill block of the given size.
Returns the address range of this defined addressable.
Get the content for this block. Block must not be a zero-fill block.
Set the content for this block.

detaileddescription.para: Caller is responsible for ensuring the underlying bytes are not deallocated while pointed to by this block.

briefdescription.para: Get mutable content for this block.

detaileddescription.para: If this Block's content is not already mutable this will trigger a copy of the existing immutable content to a new, mutable buffer allocated using LinkGraph::allocateContent.

briefdescription.para: Get mutable content for this block.

detaileddescription.para: This block's content must already be mutable. It is a programmatic error to call this on a block with immutable content consider using getMutableContent instead.

briefdescription.para: Set mutable content for this block.

detaileddescription.para: The caller is responsible for ensuring that the memory pointed to by MutableContent is not deallocated while pointed to by this block.

briefdescription.para: Returns true if this block's content is mutable.

detaileddescription.para: This is primarily useful for asserting that a block is already in a mutable state prior to modifying the content. E.g. when applying fixups we expect the block to already be mutable as it should have been copied to working memory.

briefdescription.para: Get the alignment for this content.
Set the alignment for this content.
Get the alignment offset for this content.
Set the alignment offset for this content.

briefdescription.para: Add an edge to this block.
Add an edge by copying an existing one.

detaileddescription.para: This is typically used when moving edges between blocks.

briefdescription.para: Return the list of edges attached to this content.
Returns the list of edges attached to this content.
Returns an iterator over all edges at the given offset within the block.
Returns an iterator over all edges at the given offset within the block.
Return the size of the edges list.
Returns true if the list of edges is empty.
Remove the edge pointed to by the given iterator.

detaileddescription.para: Returns an iterator to the new next element.

briefdescription.para: Returns the address of the fixup for the given edge, which is equal to this block's address plus the edge's offset.
An Addressable with content and edges.
